transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-15 14:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Park (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood Solutions), Ravi Menon (Phoenix Arc - Head of Cloud Partnerships), Sasha Ivanov (Phoenix Arc - Senior DevOps), Priya Kapoor (Phoenix Arc - PM)

Summary: quick technical kickoff to align on the Phoenix Arc marketplace listing and private connectivity runbook. Focus areas: packaging (helm + marketplace artifact), VPC/KMS compatibility, onprem vs VPC deployment patterns, quant/latency tradeoffs, and a plan for a Redwood-hosted benchmark lab.

Topics: listing packaging, VPC peering and NAT restrictions, KMS key policy and HSM note, runtime quantization and perf expectations, telemetry/trace integration, canary rollout plan.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining — should we do quick intros?
[00:12] Ravi: yeah hi I m ravi, i run partnerships at Phoenix Arc, we re the cloud-native edge platform, we're trying to list a managed connector in your marketplace.
[00:20] Maya: awesome thanks Ravi. devon and lena from our side, devon leads the integration patterns, lena helps with packaging and docs.
[00:30] Devon: hey all.
[00:35] Sasha: Sasha here, devops, i m the one who will actually wire up the networking and tekton jobs.
[00:40] Priya: priya, product, i m owning go-to-market success.

[02:05] Maya: high level agenda — packaging checklist, networking/VPC requirements, KMS and audit logs, perf expectations and quant, and lab/benchmark next steps. sound good?
[02:15] Ravi: yep works. may i add scope of what success looks like: fastest 99th p95 under 250ms for small request patterns and deterministic cost under our reserved capacity — those are-ish our goals.
[02:30] Devon: ok quick note, those tail lat targets depend a lot on sequence length, batching and whether you want prefix KV caching. we ll talk through compatible model variants and quantization options.

[05:00] Maya: packaging first — phoenix arc wants to ship an onprem connector that can be listed in Redwood's marketplace. typical pattern: we publish a listing that pulls a Helm chart + values file, and an optional operator. the listing page can surface region, support matrix, and a container image URI.
[05:18] Priya: question: do we need to provide an operator? our team would prefer a simple helm chart + kube manifests if possible.
[05:26] Lena: you can do helm-only. operator is optional for lifecycle automation, but helm values should include KMS config placeholders and nodeSelector/taints for dedicated pools.
[06:10] Sasha: for security we have strict egress rules — no outbound to internet except a proxy. will the marketplace installer need to reach redwood control plane?
[06:25] Devon: good point. for Private deployments you can opt into a customer-managed control plane or use our lightweight inbound-only connector. we have both patterns: 1) VPC peering + internal endpoints, 2) outbound-only via customer proxy with mTLS. the installer can be offline if you provide the bundle.
[06:50] Ravi: bundle sounds appealing. can you share checksum/signature patterns?
[06:56] Lena: yes we sign release tarballs; we also publish SHA256 and provenance docs. we'll include a sample verify script.

[08:20] Maya: KMS — we support AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault, and generic customer HSM via PKCS#11. what does phoenix arc expect?
[08:30] Sasha: we use AWS KMS, but our security requires specific IAM policies and separate keys per environment. we also need audit log hooks to our SIEM.
[08:45] Devon: Redwood's private runtime accepts KMS key ARNs and supports envelope encryption. we can add KMS policy examples; note we also support a caching tier for token keys — but that has tradeoffs for key rotation.
[09:05] Priya: are audit logs exported? can we route them to our Splunk or S3?
[09:12] Lena: yes logs and telemetry can be forwarder to S3, Splunk, or Datadog — we provide an opentelemetry collector config in the helm chart.

[10:40] Devon: switching to perf and quant — if you're targeting <250ms for short inferences, recommended pattern is 8-bit quantized weights on A100 or equivalent, sequence length trimmed, and per-customer dedicated pool for predictable tail. gf (glitch): sorry, A100 i mean A100S / L40x.
[11:05] Ravi: ok is 8-bit always safe for our use case? we have some reasoning tasks.
[11:12] Devon: 8-bit QAT is usually fine, but we should run the evals. we ll propose a small prompt set to validate accuracy drop; Redwood Optimize can provide a delta report.
[11:30] Maya: another option is model routing: use a cheaper quant variant for low-priority queries and fallback to higher-precision for high-confidence scoring. that helps cost.

[13:00] Sasha: network — our infra spans multiple VPCs and strict NAT gateways. any issues with egress SNAT port exhaustion if you have many concurrent connections?
[13:15] Devon: yes that can hit you; we recommend connection pooling and a sidecar proxy that multiplexes requests. our helm chart has an envoy sidecar example and settings for connection reuse.
[13:35] Priya: is there a guidance doc for connection pool settings?
[13:40] Lena: we'll share a default values.yaml with pool sizes tuned for common cluster sizes. we also include a helper script to generate iptables rules for SNAT reduction.

[15:05] Maya: telemetry — we need to capture token-level cost and latency per route, redwood will provide a tokenized costs CSV export and an otel span tag for model_version. do you need anything else?
[15:20] Ravi: we need SSO user mapping for RBAC in the marketplace — mapping between Phoenix Arc tenant IDs and our product roles.
[15:28] Devon: our listing abstracts a tenant binding step — we'll provide SAML metadata and an API endpoint for tenant onboarding. there is a one-time handshake.

[17:45] Sasha: about canaries and rollouts — our org policy requires gradual rollout with automatic rollback if error rate > 2%. can the marketplace listing support canary and A/B?
[17:58] Lena: yes, Redwood Console supports canary rollouts by weight and you can configure alerts. we'll include a sample rollout policy and a webhook for your automation to trigger rollback.

[19:30] Priya: Ok let's talk security questionnaire items — SOC2 and ISO — we will need SOC2 Type II and evidence of key rotation. are you SOC2?
[19:42] Maya: yes Redwood is SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified. we can share the attestation and a redacted SOC2 report under NDA.
[19:55] Ravi: perfect, we'll sign NDA for the report.

[21:20] Devon: technical nit — on CPU vs GPU split for the connector's control plane. our operator expects small CPU footprint and offloads tokens to the GPU nodes, but some telemetry processing uses CPU. tune node affinitiy in values.yaml.
[21:35] Sasha: anything special for noisy-neighbor mitigation? we run multi-tenant clusters.
[21:42] Devon: set resource quotas per namespace and enable per-tenant cgroups on the GPU scheduler — we supply a scheduler plugin example.

[24:00] Maya: now the benchmarking lab: we propose Redwood hosts a short perf lab where we run your workload against a dedicated test cluster using our standard and a quant profile. goal to produce a delta table: p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec and cost-per-1000 tokens. can you commit to a small prompt set?
[24:18] Priya: yes, we'll assemble 30-40 production-like prompts covering short/long contexts and LLM-critical flows.
[24:25] Devon: great, i'll prepare a perf harness and lightweight script that can run both in our lab and yours.

[26:40] Ravi: curious — what telemetry fields are mandatory for the lab?
[26:48] Lena: minimal: model_version, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, route_id, tenant_id (redacted ok), and error code. optional: embedding dims, quant_profile.

[28:10] Sasha: rain check: we have an L3 compliance gate requiring HSM attestation for high-sensitivity workloads. does Redwood integrate with external HSMs?
[28:22] Devon: yes via PKCS#11 and our key wrapping layer. for attestation we'll need to coordinate keys exchange and provide an HSM-compatible config. note: performance impact ~5–10% due to cryptographic ops on per-request envelope decryption.

[30:00] Maya: timeline and milestones — short term: share listing checklist and helm sample (by Nov 17), collect VPC/CIDR/KMS details (Phoenix Arc by Nov 20), run Redwood lab week of Nov 29, follow-up integration sprint in early Dec. does that align?
[30:20] Ravi: yes aligns.

[31:50] Priya: pricing and reserved capacity — curious what inputs you need to model committed throughput?
[31:58] Devon: we'll need expected qps, average tokens per request, peak concurrency window, and acceptable SLOs. using that we produce a sizing and cost recommendation for Dedicated vs Burst.

[33:30] Sasha: are there export controls or geo-residency constraints we should be aware of? we operate in eu-west and ap-south.
[33:40] Maya: Redwood supports region pinning and data residency; for EU we can host the runtime in eu-west exclusively and use regional control plane or private deployments. we ll document that.

[35:10] Ravi: any notable competitors feature we should call out? we heard TritonAI has a one-click operator but limited quant options.
[35:22] Devon: yes Triton has good operator UX, but our differentiation is the unified routing and cost controls across hosted/dedicated/private with bake-in canaries and rollout.

[37:00] Maya: Docs & artifacts we'll share: helm chart repo link, marketplace packaging checklist, sample values, opentelemetry collector config, perf harness and a template prompt set.
[37:12] Lena: also a checklist for KMS policies and sample IAM JSONs.

[38:45] Priya: ok on legal — Phoenix Arc needs marketplace terms: is there a standard partner contract?
[38:55] Maya: yes our partnerships team has an MPA template, we ll introduce legal contacts separately; for the listing there's a lightweight Marketplace Listing Agreement.

[40:20] Ravi: any gotchas you typically see in private deployments?
[40:28] Devon: common ones: (1) SNAT exhaustion, (2) mismatched KMS permissions, (3) insufficient node labeling for GPU scheduling; we 'll annotate the helm values with checks.

[42:10] Sasha: about images — we prefer to host images in our internal registry. can the listing point to your canonical image or our internal mirror?
[42:22] Lena: both. listing can reference upstream images and we support an airgap/mirrored bundle with documented import steps.

[44:00] Maya: open Qs — Ravi, any internal stakeholders we should bring in next week?
[44:10] Ravi: yes, i'll loop in legal and our platform lead (Katerina) to the Nov 29 bench kickoff.

[45:30] Devon: i'll also draft a lightweight runbook for canary rollback sequences with example Prometheus alerts.

[46:45] Maya: let me recap next steps — Maya send listing checklist + helm sample (Nov 17), Phoenix Arc provide VPC + KMS details (Nov 20), Redwood run perf lab week of Nov 29 and share results, devon to prepare perf harness by Nov 24, legal intro and SOC2 NDA.

[48:00] Priya: great thank you. any final concerns?
[48:08] Sasha: just to emphasize SNAT mitigation script, please include iptables helper.
[48:14] Lena: yes will include it.

[49:40] Ravi: thanks everybody this was helpful.
[49:45] Maya: thank you all — we ll follow up in email with links and the checklist.
[50:00] End.

Notes: transcript includes typical filler and minor transcribe errors; names sometimes run together in audio. Reference artifacts mentioned: /docs/marketplace/packaging-checklist.md (will be shared), helm chart repo https://github.com/redwood-inference/partner-helm-samples (sample), perf harness gist link to be created.
